title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
grouping: Three rounded, black-outlined panels with tab-style labels on their top edge: (a) a strip of images across the top-left, (b) a transformer block at top-right, (c) a wide step-by-step strip across the bottom. A wedge drawn from the module in (b) widens into panel (c), marking it as that module's inside.
shapes_depth: Panel (a) shows the input photo then four versions of it overlaid with coloured patch outlines whose groups grow coarser per block. Panel (b) is a flat block diagram: tall grey pill for input and output, pale red rounded 'Attention' box, pale green 'MLP' box, small circled-plus residual nodes and a light-blue trapezoid narrowing in the flow direction for the merging step. Panel (c) draws tokens as two columns of small circles, red for one set and blue for the other, with grey lines for candidate matches and darker lines for kept ones; merged tokens become overlapping circles, purple where a red and blue merged. Each step has a bold 'Step N:' caption with the set names in their colour.
proposed_highlight: The added module is the light-blue trapezoid labelled with the method name inside an otherwise standard block, and the zoom wedge expands it into its own five-step panel; the title spells the name with bold initials ('To'ken 'Me'rging).
lesson: Draw a token-reduction module as a trapezoid that narrows in the flow direction, then zoom it into a step strip where tokens are two-colour circles that visibly fuse into overlapping mixed-colour circles.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'). Panel (a) holds an embedded photo with patch overlays.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: faster ViT inference by token merging

core.what: the widest panel, (c) Bipartite Soft Matching, runs the algorithm on a toy set of eleven token circles in five steps left to right: split into red Set A and blue Set B columns, draw each A token's edge to its most similar B token, keep the top r edges, merge the connected pairs, concatenate - each step captioned beneath

relations.form: token circles in two facing columns with straight edges between them; kept edges drawn dark and dropped ones light grey; merged tokens drawn as overlapping red-blue circles and then as purple circles
five step columns in one row inside panel (c), joined by straight black arrows, each with a bold 'Step n:' caption under it
the blue ToMe trapezoid in panel (b) widens into a callout wedge that opens down onto panel (c), tying the operation to the block it lives in
panel (b) is one horizontal block: X -> pink Attention -> residual + -> blue ToMe -> green MLP -> residual + -> Y, with residual lines running beneath
panel (a) shows a dog photo, then the same photo with patch outlines after patchifying and after blocks 11, 22 and 32, coloured outlines growing as tokens merge

channels.colour: red = Set A tokens, blue = Set B tokens, purple = merged tokens (the mix of the two) in panel (c); in panel (b) blue also fills the ToMe trapezoid and pink/green fill Attention/MLP, so blue carries two meanings; outline colours in panel (a) only separate merged groups
channels.shape: circles = tokens; a trapezoid narrowing to the right = ToMe (fewer tokens out); rounded rectangles = transformer sub-layers; small circled plus = residual addition
channels.line: black arrows = step order and data flow; straight edges = similarity matches, dark = kept, light grey = dropped
channels.frame: three rounded panels with tab labels a), b), c), the zoom wedge joining b) to c)

quality.strengths: the new operation is the biggest panel and is drawn as geometry on a small instance - the reader watches edges appear, get pruned to the top r and collapse into purple merged tokens, so bipartite matching is understood without the text; the trapezoid shape for ToMe says 'fewer tokens out' and the callout wedge places it inside the block; panel (a) shows the effect on a real image at three depths
quality.weaknesses: blue means both Set B tokens and the ToMe block; in Step 4 the merged pairs are drawn as overlapping circles that are easy to misread as three tokens; panel (a)'s coloured patch outlines are not explained, so the grouping they show must be inferred

insights.structure: Three rounded panels with tab labels: (a) a photo strip top-left, (b) a transformer block top-right with the new ToMe trapezoid between Attention and MLP, and (c) a full-width five-step strip below that a wedge from the ToMe box opens into.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as two columns of small circles (red Set A, blue Set B) with grey candidate edges and dark kept edges; merged tokens become overlapping circles that turn purple, while (a) shows the real dog photo with coloured patch outlines that coarsen from Patchfied to Block 32.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only light-blue trapezoid in panel (b), narrowing in the flow direction, and the zoom wedge from it makes the whole bottom panel its explanation; the title bolds 'To' and 'Me'.
insights.flow: Panels (a) and (b) read left to right on the top row, then the wedge drops the eye into (c), whose steps run left to right joined by black arrows, each with a bold 'Step N:' caption underneath.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) has no arrows or link to (b), so the reader must infer that the merging snapshots are produced by stacking the block in (b).

arrangement.units: three black-outlined rounded panels with tab titles (a) result strip, (b) block diagram, (c) algorithm steps; (c) is a zoom of the ToMe box in (b)
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo at the left of panel (a); x as a grey pill at the left of (b)
